title: Jev patch version accepted by one validator, not the other

request.goal: With default RunConfig, Gateway.call sends a valid Jev request for model "typesafe/jev-1.13". OpenRouter answers with model "jev-1.13.2" and otherwise valid usage, cost and answers. Would jev_decide.validate_response alone accept this model? What error code does the Gateway record for the call?

identity.title: scripts/transport.py excerpt (_validate_identity)
identity.text:
def _validate_identity(self, role, response, payload):
        returned = response.get("model")
        require(isinstance(returned, str), "missing_response_model")
        normalized = "typesafe/" + returned.removeprefix("typesafe/") if role == "jev" else returned
        require(normalized in self.config.response_models(role, payload["model"]), "response_model_mismatch")

config.title: scripts/config.py excerpt (aliases and response_models)

jev.title: scripts/jev_decide.py excerpt (validate_response model check)
jev.text:
requested = request["model"].removeprefix("~").removeprefix("typesafe/")
    returned = response["model"].removeprefix("typesafe/")
    require(re.fullmatch(r"jev-[A-Za-z0-9._-]+", returned) and
            (requested == "jev-latest" or returned == requested or
             returned.startswith((requested + ".", requested + "-"))), "response_model_mismatch")

pass: validate_response alone would accept it ("jev-1.13.2" starts with "jev-1.13."), but the Gateway normalizes it to "typesafe/jev-1.13.2", which is neither jev_model nor the alias, so the event records response_model_mismatch (and call() then raises provider_call_failed).
fail: Both accept it: it is a dotted patch of the requested version.
jev_decide rejects it; the Gateway accepts it as an alias and the call succeeds.
